key_insight: HVOF-deposited WC-17Co coatings retain their best dry-sliding wear performance at 200–400 °C, with a clear optimum around 400 °C before wear worsens at higher temperatures.
engineering_relevance: For high-temperature wear applications, WC-17Co HVOF coatings can be selected for moderate thermal exposure, but designs should avoid sustained operation above 400 °C due to oxidation and binder degradation.
method: Deposited WC-17Co coating by HVOF and tested dry sliding wear from room temperature to 600 °C under constant load and speed.
Characterized coating and wear tracks using SEM, EDS, XRD, and 3D surface profilometry.
Compared morphology, phase stability, and wear-track geometry before and after testing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~268.99 μm coating thickness, 1.53% porosity, and minimum wear/friction at 400 °C, while wear increases sharply at 500–600 °C.
watch_item: The favorable wear window is temperature-sensitive, so real service conditions with longer exposure, different loads, or harsher oxidation may reduce the coating’s performance.
paper_title: Effect of thermal exposure on the wear and phase stability of HVOF-deposited WC-17Co coatings
